metadata.description: A software component as a fact: a library, an application, an operating system or a firmware build. One record per purl, shared by every SoftwareBillOfMaterials that lists it. A Knowledge class: discovered by a scanner sweep, never provider-realized. Package URL, CPE and SPDX/CycloneDX component identity are adopted by reference; the purl is the portable correlation id. Listed by SoftwareBillOfMaterials; references Vulnerability.

purl.description: Package URL, the portable identity and dedup key (pkg:maven/org.apache.logging.log4j/log4j-core@2.14.1). One record per purl.

license.description: Declared license as an SPDX identifier (Apache-2.0), where the SBOM reports one.

cpe.description: The CPE 2.3 name of the component, where one is assigned. It is the identifier a vulnerability database matches an operating system, an appliance or a firmware build by, where no package ecosystem gives one. A second correlation id beside the purl, never a replacement for it.

component_type.description: What kind of component this is, as the bill of materials reports it: the CycloneDX component type, adopted by reference. It tells a reader whether a fix is a package update, an image rebuild or a firmware flash. Absent means the document did not say.

relationships.name: affected_by
relationships.description: affected_by — this package version is affected by the vulnerability (OSV / VEX). A declarative typed reference; the match is Policy. Non-ordering, but walked by blast-radius/impact in reverse (the CVE -> resource path).

adopts.role: the canonical package identifier this type's identity fields carry
SBOM interchange alignment; license identifiers use the SPDX license list
SBOM interchange alignment (component identity and references)
the second component identifier, for operating systems, appliances and firmware that a vulnerability database names by CPE

context.purpose: Records a software component as one shared fact per package URL, so every bill of materials that lists it points at the same record.
context.plain_description: One component at one version — a library, an application, an operating system release or a firmware build — identified by its purl (Package URL), the portable id that carries ecosystem, name, and version in one string. Firmware and appliances with no package ecosystem use the `generic` purl type and carry a `cpe`, the name a vulnerability database knows them by. There is exactly one record per purl no matter how many documents list it, which is what makes blast-radius questions cheap: find the package once, walk back to every image, host and device that carries it. Discovered by scanners; never built or provisioned.
use_when: You need where-do-we-run-version-X-of-library-Y answerable as a graph walk.
You need packages linked to the advisories affecting them.
not_for: The image or host carrying the package — its SoftwareBillOfMaterials lists packages.
The advisory itself — Vulnerability; a package is affected_by it.
works_with: SoftwareBillOfMaterials — the documents that list this package, each about one image, host or device.
Vulnerability — the advisories affecting this package version.
